title: How does dependency injection work?
keyPoints: IoC container manages object creation and wiring instead of manual new
Constructor injection preferred over field injection for immutability and testability
Beans resolved by type, disambiguated with @Qualifier or @Primary
Reduces coupling between components and eases mocking in tests

title: Explain the bean lifecycle
keyPoints: Instantiate, populate properties, apply Aware interfaces, then init callbacks
@PostConstruct / afterPropertiesSet run before the bean is ready for use
@PreDestroy runs on container shutdown for cleanup
Scope affects lifecycle: singleton (default, one per container) vs prototype (new per request)

title: How do you manage configuration?
keyPoints: Externalize config via application.yml/properties with profiles (dev/prod)
@ConfigurationProperties for typed, validated config binding
@Value for injecting individual properties
Environment variables or a config server can override per environment

title: How should REST controllers be structured?
keyPoints: Keep controllers thin, delegate business logic to the service layer
Use proper HTTP verbs/status codes
Use DTOs instead of exposing entities directly
Have a clear API versioning strategy

title: How do you validate requests?
keyPoints: Bean Validation annotations (@NotNull, @Size, @Email) on DTOs
@Valid/@Validated on controller parameters triggers validation
Custom validators via ConstraintValidator for domain-specific rules
Handle validation errors centrally via @ExceptionHandler / MethodArgumentNotValidException

title: How do you handle API exceptions?
keyPoints: @ControllerAdvice + @ExceptionHandler for centralized error handling
Map exceptions to appropriate HTTP status codes and a structured error response
Avoid leaking stack traces or internal details to clients
Use a custom exception hierarchy for domain-specific errors

title: How does Spring Data derive queries?
keyPoints: Method name parsing (findByXAndY) generates queries automatically
@Query for custom JPQL/SQL when method-name derivation isn't enough
Repository interfaces extend JpaRepository/CrudRepository with no implementation needed
Paging and sorting supported via a Pageable parameter

title: What does @Transactional do?
keyPoints: Wraps a method in a database transaction, commits on success
Rolls back by default on unchecked/runtime exceptions only
Propagation controls how transactions nest (REQUIRED, REQUIRES_NEW, etc.)
Proxy-based: self-invocation within the same class bypasses @Transactional

title: How do you secure an API?
keyPoints: Spring Security filter chain intercepts requests for authentication/authorization
Stateless APIs typically use JWT/OAuth2 tokens instead of sessions
Method-level security via @PreAuthorize/@Secured
CORS/CSRF configuration appropriate to API vs browser-form usage

title: How do you test a Spring Boot service?
keyPoints: @SpringBootTest for full context integration tests, @WebMvcTest for a controller slice
Mock dependencies with @MockBean, verify HTTP layer with MockMvc
Use Testcontainers for real database-backed integration tests
Prefer plain Mockito unit tests over loading the full context when possible
